scope: Existing endpoints only; four bounded methods proposals, no canonical application.

proposals.relationship: Le Goff criticizes a tendency toward immobility in Braudelian history while retaining and extending its analysis of historical rhythms.
proposals.evidence_note: Le Goff’s own answer in the December 1988 interview, published in Spanish in 1991, criticizes a partial neglect of change. He expressly says neither Braudel nor Le Roy Ladurie actually wrote a truly immobile history, then describes a generalization of Braudel’s rhythms. This qualified criticism does not cancel the separately documented positive spatial debt. Braudel’s 1958 essay is discussed here through Le Goff’s testimony, not newly read.
primary_locators: Printed pp.59–60; PDF pages4–5, question on immobile time and Le Goff’s two following answers

proposals.relationship: Le Goff names Duby’s book on Bouvines as an exemplary way to write renewed event history.
proposals.evidence_note: In his own answer, Le Goff calls this a repeatedly cited successful example while discussing how to renew political and event history. This records a specific praised methodological model, not a comprehensive formative debt or an endorsement of all Duby’s arguments. Duby’s book was not newly read. This differs from Le Goff’s separate qualified criticism of Duby’s presentation of women.
primary_locators: Printed p.61; PDF page6, Le Goff’s answer immediately after the question on events as an indication of structures

proposals.relationship: Le Goff explicitly credits Chartier, alongside Jacques Revel, with collaboration essential to the original La Nouvelle Histoire project of 1978.
proposals.evidence_note: Le Goff’s 1988 acknowledgments and opening preface credit both collaborators. This is a contribution to a specified joint editorial project, not intellectual descent or sole authorship by Chartier. The 1988 abridged, updated collection is distinguished from the 1978 encyclopedia. Only the selected primary frontmatter transcription was read; the complete book and individual contributors’ essays were not newly read.
primary_locators: Unnumbered acknowledgments; “Préface à la nouvelle édition (1988),” printed p.9, opening paragraph

proposals.relationship: Schmitt attributes Le Goff’s reorientation toward medieval historical anthropology partly to the expanding influence of Lévi-Strauss’s structural anthropology.
proposals.evidence_note: This is explicitly Jean-Claude Schmitt’s named account reproduced by EPHE. It concerns the reorientation of Le Goff’s direction of studies, with other anthropologists also credited; it does not establish personal mentorship, a joint project, exclusive influence or wholesale adoption of structuralism. The passage is not Le Goff’s own acknowledgment. The Clio interview’s distinct Lévi-Strauss passage concerns Duby and is not used to infer this relationship.
primary_locators: “Domaines de recherches,” first Schmitt-attributed paragraph, beginning with the earlier “sociologie historique” title
